newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS - Manila stocks bounce back but not yet out of woods.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Manila stocks bounce back but not yet out of woods.

text.p: Philippine shares broke out of a seven-day slump and ended higher on Thursday as bargain hunters snapped up battered property issues but analysts said the market was not yet out of the woods.
Bursts of applause rang through the trading floor of the Philippine Stock Exchange as the market stirred back to life and the main index finished 39.72 points, or 1.37 percent, up at 2,949.02 points.
The index, representing a basket of 30 companies, had lost 9.73 percent since it began sinking on March 31 in its worst downturn in nearly six months on fears of a property crash due to a glut.
"It's too early to rejoice," said Louie Bate, managing director for Equities Brokerage Trading at ING Baring Securities Philippines Inc.
"It's too early to discount the bears out. It could (today's rise) just be a dead cat's bounce," he said.
Cilette Liboro, research head of Citisecurities Inc, viewed the day's rebound as "just a technical rally borne out of short covering and some bargain hunters."
She said bargain-hunting and short covering would probably continue on Friday but the upside would be limited.
Some 3.3 billion pesos worth of shares changed hands as gainers outpaced losers 103 to 51.
All sectors from mining and oils to banks and commercial- industrial issues gained with property issues, badly pummelled by rumours since last week, spearheading the advance.
Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc gained 70 centavos to seven pesos while its mass housing unit Empire East Land Holdings Inc gained 50 centavos to 6.30 pesos.
Property developer and index heavyweight Ayala Land-B gained 50 centavos to 26 pesos while SM Prime Holdings SMPH.S also closed 50 centavos up at 7.30 pesos.

Property issues had been battered by rumours the industry might suffer the same fate that befell Thailand's property and banking sectors because of a reported glut in the local industry that investors fear could trigger a crash in prices.
A property oversupply in Thailand had badly hit Thai banks because of their huge loans to real estate firms in that country.
"I don't think the property scare is over," research head Joel Santillan of Asiamerit Securities Inc said. "I think there are some long term concerns about property."

That, along with worries about exposures of local banks to the property industry, would continue to drag the two sectors "and that should drag the market considering that property has a big weight in it," Santillan said.
Analysts said downward pressures continued to grip the market despite Thursday's gains.

"The market has been going downhill," Santillan said. "One could liken this upswing to putting on the brakes. It remains to be seen how far it will skid before we can really say the market has resumed its uptrend."
Wilfred Son Keng Po, sales and research head at Angping Securities, said he expected the market to consolidate at between 2,850 and 3,000 levels in the next few days.
"The market will look for direction to reports of the first quarter earnings of companies," he said. Corporate results are expected late this month or early next.
